newsitem.title: USA: Phillips confirms Bayu-Undan south flank.
newsitem.headline: Phillips confirms Bayu-Undan south flank.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said Tuesday a successful appraisal well in the Bayu-Undan gas/condensate field in the Timor Sea between Indonesia and Australia encountered a productive section of hydrocarbons in the southern flank of the field.

The Bayu No. 5 well was drilled on the Phillips-operated block ZOCA 91-13 to a total depth of 10,827 feet. The well encountered a 184-foot gross reservoir column with the same gas-water contact found in the previous Bayu-Undan wells.
Phillips said it did not flow-test the well because the reservoir sands encountered were fully cored.
It said the section was similar to sands successfully flow-tested elsewhere in the field. The well was drilled as an expendable appraisal well and was plugged and abandoned.

"The success of Bayu No. 5 confirms the southern extension of the Bayu-Undan reservoir and substantially completes the license group's appraisal drilling program," according to Knut Am, Phillips Petroleum Co ZOC senior vice president, exploration and production.

Am continued, "Phillips and our co-venturers plan to finalize feasibility engineering studies and select a development plan for the field by the end of March. A decision on commerciality could come by late 1997 or early 1998."

The Bayu-Undan field covers an estimated 130 square miles, Phillips said. The field's natural gas wells are located 185 miles off the northwest coast of Australia and 140 miles south of Indonesia. Block ZOCA 91-13 is in the Zone of Cooperation A, an area jointly administered by Australia and Indonesia.
Participating in ZOCA 91-13 are: Phillips, the operator, with a 60 percent interest; Oryx Energy Co, 25 percent; and Hardy Oil & Gas Plc, 15 percent.
